title: Number Bonds to 10
keyIdea: Number bonds to 10 are pairs of numbers that add to exactly 10: 1+9, 2+8, 3+7, 4+6, 5+5 and the same pairs swapped. If 7 counters fill a ten-frame, 3 spaces stay empty, so 7 and 3 are partners. Knowing these pairs lets you make 10 quickly without counting every time.

kid: Some pairs of numbers add to 10. We call them number bonds to 10.
Put 7 counters in a ten-frame. Count the empty spaces. There are 3. So 7 and 3 are partners: 7 + 3 = 10.
Other pairs: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 4 + 6, 5 + 5. Swap them and they still make 10: 9 + 1, 8 + 2, and so on.
When you see 6 + □ = 10, the empty box needs 4, because 6 and 4 are a bond to 10.
adult: Reception and Year 1 number bonds ask children to find the number that makes 10 with a given 1-9 (CCSS K.OA.4; NC Y1 number bonds to 10). The catalog topic is named 'Number bonds to 9' but the evidence is bonds to 10 — partners of 1 through 9. Teach bonds to 10.

Words to use: number bond, partner, ten-frame, make 10, pair, equation. Common mistakes: giving the same number again (7 needs 7); adding to a teen (7 + 7 = 14); sticking digits (5 + 5 read as 55); forgetting 5 + 5 and 10 + 0.
In the lab your child fills a ten-frame, counts empty spaces, matches partners, completes equations and snaps quick bonds.

familyTip: Play 'I say 7, you say…' and wait for 3. Use fingers: hold up 4 and ask how many more fingers make 10. A muffin tin with 10 cups works as a giant ten-frame.
